The inverse scattering problem aims to determine the shape of a perfect conductor from scattered electromagnetic waves generated by time-harmonic plane waves.
The linear sampling method is a linear algorithm that does not require knowledge of boundary conditions or weak scattering assumptions.
The method traditionally requires multi-static data over the full unit sphere and fails at eigenvalues of an interior boundary value problem.
Using combined far-field operators from electric and magnetic scattered fields overcomes the eigenvalue problem.
Combined far-field operator F is defined as Fg(x̂) = α ∫ E∞(x̂; d) g(d) ds(d) + β ∫ H∞(x̂; d) g(d) ds(d), with α > 0 and β < 0 real constants.
Herglotz wave functions with L2 kernels are used to represent incident fields and approximate interior solutions.
The range of the operator B mapping boundary data to far-field patterns is dense in L2 of the unit sphere.
The transmission problem (TP) couples interior and exterior Helmholtz equations with boundary conditions linking the fields.
The linear sampling method with combined far-field data is valid for all positive wave numbers k, without restrictions on eigenvalues.
Limited aperture data suffices for reconstruction since Herglotz wave functions can be approximated by kernels supported on subsets of the unit sphere.
The paper treats both 2D scattering by an infinite cylinder and 3D scattering by bounded obstacles with Lipschitz boundaries.
The electric field satisfies a Dirichlet boundary condition (tangential component zero) on the perfect conductor surface.
The magnetic field satisfies a Neumann boundary condition on the boundary in the 2D scalar case.
Regularization methods such as Tikhonov regularization are used to solve the far-field equation approximately when the sampling point is outside the scatterer.
As the sampling point approaches the scatterer boundary, the norm of the solution to the far-field equation and the corresponding Herglotz wave function become unbounded.
The Silver-Müller radiation condition is imposed on the scattered fields in the 3D vector case.
The incident electromagnetic plane wave is represented by vector potentials involving polarization vectors and propagation directions.
The paper relies on new approximation properties of electromagnetic Herglotz pairs developed in earlier works.
The factorization of the modified far-field operator is essential for the analysis and is more involved than in previous scalar cases.
The approach to eliminate eigenvalue difficulties relies heavily on polarization effects and is specific to electromagnetic scattering.
